clinician.trajectory_summary: A 2-day-old Caucasian female was transferred from maternity to the hospital presenting with reverse peristalsis, significant abdominal distention, inability to pass stools, and fever. Initial rectal stimulation resulted in defecation and symptom improvement, but the patient remained unable to pass stools without stimulation. Rectal examination revealed an empty rectum with no explosive gas/fluid release. Contrast enema on day 4 showed absence of a transition zone, suggesting extensive colonic involvement. A first rectal biopsy on day 10 was non-diagnostic. Approximately one month later, plain radiography demonstrated extensive colonic and intestinal flatulence. Before surgical intervention, per oral contrast radiography showed extreme meteorism, Kloiber cups, and signs of megacolon. On day 75, an enterostomy was performed, and full-thickness biopsy specimens from the rectum and colon were obtained and subjected to histology and immunohistology staining, confirming the diagnosis of total colonic aganglionosis.
